issues.legal_issue: Property allotted collectively to a female and her existing thavazhi on partition retains its tharwad character.
Property allotted on partition to a single female without living descendants is her separate property and does not become tharwad property merely because she later has children.
A mother who becomes the absolute owner of property on her son’s death may transfer the entire property by mortgage to her daughter-in-law and grandchildren.
The Supreme Court may interfere with concurrent findings of fact only in exceptional circumstances warranting use of its discretionary jurisdiction.
The rule that a single female’s partition allotment is separate property applies prospectively and does not disturb concluded or ongoing transactions.
